λαβαντίς.definition: name of a vegetable, gloss on Id

λαβδακισμός.definition: a defect in pronunciation, Quint.Inst.1.5.32 , Diom.453 K

λαβδοειδής.definition: formed like a the os hyoïdes, Gal.18.957, Orib.25.8.1; the suture in the skull between the occiput and sinciput, Gal.UP9.5, Ruf.Onom.133; Theol.Ar.3

λαβράνιος.definition: epith. of Zeus in Cyprus, Myres Cesnola Collection p.550

λάβραξ.definition: a ravenous sea-fish, Labrax lupus, the bass, Alc.107, Eup.150 , Diph.66.10, Arist.HA567a19, 591a11, Ptol.Euerg.1 J.; Ar.Fr.595; prov. of greedy persons, Apostol.10.38, cf. Ar.Eq.361

λαβρώνιος.definition: large wide cup, Men.503, Diph.80.1:—also Eust.1066.3; Men.24.4, Hsch. ; cf

λάγανον.definition: a thin broad cake, of meal and oil, like Diocl.Fr.116; LXXLe.2.4, cf. MatroParod.Fr.4, Gal.6.492, POxy.1211.5 , Ar.Ec.843 as cited by Ath.3.110a ; J.AJ7.4.2 ; cf. Lat. tracta, Chrysipp.Tyan. ap. Ath.14.647e:— Dim. Id.…

λαγανοφακῆ.definition: lentil pudding or cake, Bilabel p.11

λαγαρότης.definition: slackness, Hld.9.15, Anon. ap; of a verse, v. foreg. 4, Eust.1464.63

λαγέτας.definition: Dor. leader of the people, Pi.O.1.89, P.4.107, S.Fr.221.12, Hsch

λάγιον.definition: or a kind of cup or vase, Inscr.Délos 399B 149, 461Bb40, al

λαγκία.definition: Lat. lancea, D.S.5.30:—hence lancearius, CIG4004 , Lyd.Mag.1.46

λαγώειος.definition: of or belonging to a hare, Opp.C.1.491, 519

λαγών.definition: also Hp.Int.25, Aret.SD2.11; metaph., any hollow, hollow of a cup, Eub.43; AP6.326 ; Plu.Arat.22; esp. of a mountain, flank, D.H.3.24, 9.23, Cleom.1.8, Call.Fr.185 ; bank of a river, . . AP6.287 ; sides of a grave, IG…

λαγῷος.definition: contr. for of the hare, Ar.Ach.1110; Plu.2.138f; hare's flesh, Hp.Vict.2.46: and generally, dainties, delicacies, Ar.V.709, cf. Ach.1006, Pax1196, Telecl.32, Pl.Com.174.10, etc

λαγώφθαλμος.definition: lit. hare-eyed: hence, unable to close the eye, owing to shortening of the upper eyelid, Dem. Ophth. ap. Aët.7.75, cf. Gal.14.681, Aët.7.2, Paul.Aeg.6.10; v. Eust.812.2; this condition of eyes, Gal.19.439

λαέρκινον.definition: name of the plant at Side in Pamphylia, Gal.14.72

λαέρτης.definition: a kind of ant, Ael.NA10.42; a kind of; as pr. n., Laertes, the father of Odysseus, Od.1.430, al.:—also S.Ph.87, 417, etc.; ib.402 , 1286, Aj.1, etc

λαθίπονος.definition: a life forgetting, i.e. free from, pain, Id.Tr.1021

λαθυρίς.definition: caper spurge, Euphorbia Lathyris, Dsc.4.166, Gal.12.56, 14.208, al

λάθυρος.definition: kind of pulse, chickling, Lathyrus sativus, Anaxandr.41.43 , Alex.162.12 , Thphr.HP8.3.1, Plu.2.286e: heterocl. pl. Babr.74.6

λαίθαργος.definition: said to mean biting secretly , i.e. without barking, of a dog, S.Fr.885, cf. Orac. ap. Ar.Eq.1068; also, = Trag.Adesp.227: in Phryn.PSp.87 B.: Hsch

λαιμός.definition: throat, gullet, in Hom. always of men, Il.13.388; . . Od.22.15; Il.19.209; 18.34: metaph., neck of a bottle, AP9.232 : also in pl., E.Ph.1092; so of animals, Id.Supp.1201, Ar.Av.1560.—Rare in early Prose, as Hp.Cord.2…

λαισήϊον.definition: animal's skin with hair left on, used as a shield, Il.5.453 = 12.426, cf. Scol.28.2: used by the Cilicians, Hdt.7.91

λαῖτμα.definition: poet. Noun, depth or gulf of the sea, Od.4.504, 5.174, 9.260; Il.19.267, cf. Od.8.561; also alone, 7.35, cf. 5.409, 7.276, Theoc.13.24, A.R.1.1299

Λάκαινα.definition: fem. of prop. Laconian woman , Thgn.1002, cf. E.Hec.441, etc.: abs., of Helen, Id.Andr.486 ; title of play by Sophocles: freq., esp. in Trag., Ion. Prose, and X., as fem. Adj., = Hdt.7.235; E.Andr.151, Tr.1110 , Hel.1…

λακάρα.definition: or a tree, prob. bird-cherry, Prunus avium, Thphr.HP3.3.1, 3.6.1; vv.ll. in Hsch. also

λακέρνιον.definition: Dim. of Lat. lacerna, cloak, Fouilles de Doura-Europos378

λάκημα.definition: fragment broken off, PLeid.V.6.22; cleft, Zos.Alch.p.186 B.; dub. sens. in Sammelb.4425 xi 24 , BGU34 ii 3

Λάκων.definition: a Laconian or Lacedaemonian, prop; a throw of the dice, Eub.57

λάλαξ.definition: babbler, croaker: a name of the green frog , and of a bird, Hsch.; cf

λάλος.definition: talkative, babbling, loquacious, E.Supp.462, Ar.Pax653, Pl.Grg.515e, Theoc.5.75; of Argo, Orph.A.709; AP7.417.10 ; of women, dub.in Arist.Pol.1277b23; of birds, Id.HA536a24 : metaph., AP7.195 ; AJA17.162 ; of the swal…

Λαμαχίππιον.definition: burlesque word, little jockey- Lamachus, Ar.Ach.1206

Λάμια.definition: a fabulous monster said to feed on; a fierce shark, Arist.HA540b18, Gal.6.727, Plin.HN9.78; cf

λαμπάς.definition: faggot, Plb.3.93.4; any light, lamp, LXXJu.10.22; wax-light, Plu.2.263f; AP6.249 ; later of oil-lamps, Ev.Matt.25.3

λαμπηδών.definition: lustre, of the eyes, D.S.3.37; brilliance, Lib.Or.59.103; of ebony, Jul.Caes.307d

Λάμπος.definition: one of the horses of Eos, Bright, Od.23.246; cf

λάμπουρις.definition: fox, A.Fr.433, Lyc.344, 1393; v.l. for in Suid.s.v

λάμπουρος.definition: bright-tailed, epith. of foxes, Epic.Alex.Adesp.2.13; as a dog's name, Firetail, Theoc.8.65

λάμψις.definition: shining, Ph.1.72, 2.187, Gp.2.5.12: metaph., of the law, LXXBa.4.2

Λάνοτρος.definition: name of a month at Tauromenium, IG14.427 ii 1, al

λαοξόος.definition: sculptor, Ptol.Tetr.179, IG3.1308:—also ; stone-cutter, PCair.Zen.172 ; ib.176 , PTeb.121.13 , etc.:—Adj. Hsch.s.v. cf. Vett.Val.11.14

λαοτύπος.definition: cutting stones, AP7.429.3; as Subst., stone-cutter, statuary, APl.4.59

λαπαθοειδής.definition: like a dock or sorrel leaf, f.l. in Ps.-Dsc.2.166

λάπαθον.definition: monk's rhubarb, Rumex Patientia; pitfall for wild beasts, Phot., Suid.:—also Democr.122

λάπαξις.definition: Ion. evacuation of the bowels, Arist.Ph.197b24, Pr.935b30, Gal.19.199; Aret.CA2.10

λάρδος.definition: salted meat, Lyd.Mens.4.92, HeroStereom.2.54, PLond. ined.2147

λάριμνον.definition: Arabic name for frankincense, Str.16.4.19:—written by Agatharch.101

λάρινος.definition: a kind of sea-fish, Opp.H.3.399 , Hsch.:—hence = Id

λάρναξ.definition: cinerary urn or coffin, Il.24.795; . . · Th.2.34, cf. CIG4003, 4007 , 4441 , al.; the ark of Deucalion, Plu.2.968f, Luc.Syr.D.12, Apollod.1.7.2; of the Ark, AP1.62 ; esp. an ark in which children were exposed, Simon.3…

λάρος.definition: a ravenous sea-bird, perh. sea-mew, gull, Od.5.51, Arist.HA542b17, 593b3: hence, metaph., of greedy demagogues, as Cleon, Ar.Eq.956; Id.Nu.591, cf. Av.567, MatroConv.9, Timocl.4.9; also of fools, Luc.Tim.12, Sch.Ar.Pl…

λάρτιος.definition: name of a hard Rhodian stone, SIG581.98 ; IG12.2.7, cf. 677.7, 1033.22; Supp.Epigr.3.674.9

λάσαρον.definition: or = asafoetida, Hippiatr.3, Aët.1.306, 15.5, Alex.Trall.12: Dim. Aët.8.61, Gloss

λάσθη.definition: mockery, insult, = Att. Hdt.6.67, cf. AP7.345

λασιαύχην.definition: with rough, shaggy neck, of the centaur, h.Merc.224, cf. Ar.Ra.822 ; of the bear, h.Hom.7.46; of the horse, S.Ant.350 ; Theoc.25.272: also with a neut., v.l. Id.Ep.5.5

λάσιος.definition: later also Luc.Prom.12; generally, bushy, overgrown, Emp.27.2; X.HG4.2.19, cf. Pl.Cra.420e; Theoc.25.134; Id.26.3; X.Cyr.1.4.16; Id.An.6.4.26: c. dat., overgrown with . . , Luc.Prom.l.c

λασταυροκάκκαβον.definition: an aphrodisiac dish, Chrysipp. ap. Ath.1.9c

λάσταυρος.definition: epith. of a Theopomp.Hist.217 , cf. AP12.41 ; as general term of abuse, Phryn.173: is cited as a Dim. in EM159.30

Λατιάριος.definition: = Lat. Latiaris, epith. of Jupiter, D.H.4.49: the Latin festival, in honour of Jupiter Latiaris, D.C.47.40

Λατῖνος.definition: Latin, Thphr.HP5.8.1; = Lat. feriae Latinae, D.H.4.49; Str.6.1.6

Λάτμιος.definition: Latmian, , i.e. like Endymion on Latmos, Herod.8.10; cj. for in Theoc.20.39

λαυκανίη.definition: throat, Il.22.325 and prevails in later Ep., as Orph.L.554 ; Opp.H.1.755; A.R.2.192)

Λαύρειον.definition: promontory in the south of Attica, famous for its silver-mines, Hdt.7.144, Th.2.55, EM533.34, etc.; IG22.1582.67, al.; later Paus.1.1.1:—Adj. or of Mt. Laurium, Ar.Av.1106, Plu.Nic.4

Λαφρία.definition: epith. of Artemis, Paus.4.31.7, etc., cf. Str.10.2.21, Ant.Lib.40.2; of Athena, Lyc.356, etc.:—so of Hermes, Id.835

λάχανον.definition: mostly in pl., garden-herbs, opp; in pl. also, the vegetable-market, Ar.Lys.557, Alex.46.8, Diph.32.22

λάχεια.definition: obscure word read by Aristarch. in two passages of Od., . . 9.116; 10.509; expld. by Hsch., cf. Apollon.Lex., Eust.1619.30, 1667.13, Sch.; cf. Zenod. read cf.h.Ap.197

λαχειδής.definition: epith. of the toad in Nic.Al.568

Λάχεσις.definition: Ion. Lachesis, one; as Appellat., lot, destiny, Bacis ap. Hdt.9.43: pl., IG 5.602.8

λαχμός.definition: = Sch.Theoc.8.30, Eust.1521.48; v.l. for in Od.9.445, cf. Eust.1638.39, Hsch

λαχύφλοιος.definition: Nic.Al.269, expld. by Sch. as if it were cf

λέαινα.definition: fem. of lioness, Hdt.3.108: metaph; name of several salves, Orib.Fr.75, Aët.7.86, Paul.Aeg.7.17

λεβίας.definition: a kind of fish, Ar.Fr.414 , Ephipp.12.4, Diph.17.9, etc

λεγεών.definition: = Lat. legio, Ev.Matt.26.53, Ev.Marc.5.9, Plu.Rom.13, 20, IGRom.3.670, al.:—freq. written ib.214.3, al.: —hence ib.913.3, al

λειμματιαῖος.definition: in Music, of the 2, Theo Sm.p.69 H

λειμόδωρον.definition: a wild plant, prob. strangleweed, Orobanche cruenta, Thphr.CP5.15.5

λειοντοπάλης.definition: Dor. wrestler with a lion, AP9.237

λεῖος.definition: smooth to the touch, Il.4.484; in Hom., chiefly of level places or countries, Il.23.330; ib.359; Od.10.103, Hes.Op.288 ; Od.9.134; made a smooth place, Il.12.30; Hdt.2.29; Id.9.69; a smooth sea, Id.2.117; X.Ath.2.12; …

λειπογνώμων.definition: gen. lacking II.6, IG22.1357 , cf. Ister53, Poll.1.182, Luc.Lex.6, EM4.4, Hscb

λείστριον.definition: = tool for smoothing stone, IG7.3073.119, al

λειχήνωρ.definition: Lick-man, name of a mouse, Batr.202:—so also Lick-meal, name of a mouse, ib.29; Lick- platter, ib.100, 230

λειψανδρία.definition: = Hsch., v.l. in J.BJ3.3.2, for or in later Gr., Adj. Sch.E.Or.249; Verb Tz.H.1.779

λείψανον.definition: piece left, remnant; freq. in pl., remains of the dead, E.Fr.469; S.El.1113; Pl.Phd.86c; CIG 4079b , al.; but their deeds, good name, etc., E.Andr.774 ; remnants of youth, Ar.V.1066 ; sequels to . . , Longin.9.12

λειψυδρία.definition: want of water, Thphr.CP5.12.1, Plb.34.9.6, Str.16.1.10, D.S.1.52, Sammelb.4416.14 : a waterless district near Mt. Parnes in Attica, Scol.14, Hdt.5.62, Ar.Lys.665

λεκανοσκοπία.definition: Ep. the inspecting of a dish, in order to divine, Man.4.213

λεκάριον.definition: Dim. of little dish, X.Cyr.1.3.4 , Herm.Hist.2, Gal.18.240, Poll.10.86

λέκιθος.definition: gruel of pulse or cereals; yolk of an egg, Hp.Mul.2.205, freq. in Arist., as HA562a29, al.; Nic.Dam.4 J

λέκος.definition: dish, pot, pan, Demioprat. ap. Poll.10.87, Hippon.58, Phoen.2.2:—Dim. forms Epich.126, Iamb.VP26.119 ; = Hsch.; Hp. ap. Poll. l.c.:—hence a small measure or weight, Hp.Acut.63, 69; cf

λεκτίκιον.definition: Dim. of Lat.lectīca, litter, Alex. Trall.10

λέκτρον.definition: couch, bed, Hom; later, mostly in pl., marriage-bed, Pi.N.8.6 ; A.Fr.242; Id.Pers.543 ; E.Alc.925 ; Id.Med.436 ; but S.Tr.791: hence wed one, E.Med.594; etc., Id.Or.939, Hipp.944, etc.; of illicit connexions, Id.HF345…

λέμμα.definition: that which is peeled off, rind; scales, Poll.6.51

λέμυσος.definition: or Egyptian name of a kind of priest, Sammelb.1007 ; cf. PTeb.122.1

λέντιον.definition: = Lat. linteum, cloth, napkin, towel, Peripl.M.Rubr.6 , Vit.Aesop.Oxy.2083.48, Ev.Jo.13.4, Inscr.Magn.116.34, BSA 27.228 :—hence prob.attendant at the bath, IG3.1160.72, 14.2323

λέξις.definition: speech, opp. Pl.Lg.816d; diction, style, the style used here , Pl.Ap.17d; poetical diction, Id.Lg.795e, cf. Arist.Rh.1410b28, Po.1450b13, etc.; title of work by Ephorus, TheonProg.2

Λεξιφάνης.definition: Phrase-monger, title of dialogue by Lucian

λεοντοῦχος.definition: holding a lion, epith. of Asclepios at Ascalon, Marin.Procl.19

λεπαῖος.definition: of a scaur or cliff, E.Heracl.394; rocky, rugged, Id.Hipp.1248, IT324

λέπας.definition: bare rock, scaur, Simon.114.1, A.Ag.283, 298, E.Ph.24, al.; Th.7.78

λεπάς.definition: limpet, Alc.51 , Epich.42.2, 114, Hermipp.31, Arist.HA528b1, al.; Ar.V.105, cf. Pl.1096

λέπασμα.definition: coat, skin, membrane, gloss on Sch.Nic.Th.184

λεπαστή.definition: or limpet-shaped drinking-cup, Ar.Pax916, Pherecr.95, Cratin.423 :—also AJA31.349 , Hsch

λέπος.definition: rind, husk, scale, Alex.266.7, Dsc.1.40; Luc.Icar.19; Nic.Th.943; Poll.6.51, 94

λεπτότης.definition: fineness, delicacy, opp. Pl.R.523e, al.; of soil, Arr.Tact.34.1; of the air, tenuity, Pl.Ti.58b, Arist.Cael.303b24, cf. Ph.215b28: in pl., opp. Id.HA507b26; of the Epicur.Ep.1p.10U

λεπτυσμός.definition: thinning, Hp.Epid.6.3.16; Dsc.5.112; esp. of the line of battle, Ael.Tact.38.3

λεπύχανον.definition: = coat of an onion, etc., Theopomp. Com.33, Plu.2.684a, Archig. ap. Gal.12.256, 445; rind, Dsc.Eup.1.74

Λέρνα.definition: Lerna, a marsh in Argolis, the mythol. abode of the Hydra, Plu.Cleom.15, Paus.2.4.5; also Cratin.347, Str.8.6.8, etc.: gen. A.Pr.652, etc.: prov., an abyss of ills, Hsch.; so of the theatre, Cratin.l.c.:—Adj. Hes.Th.3…

λευγαλέος.definition: of persons, in sad or sorry plight, wretched, Od.16.273; 2.61. Adv. to go in ill plight, Il.13.723

Λευίτης.definition: Levite, Ev.Luc.10.32, Plu.2.671f:—fem. v.l. in J.AJ3.11.1; Ep.Hebr.7.11; title of book of VT

λευκαία.definition: = II.1, IG12.155 iii 79, iv 118:—hence Zeus of the white poplar, Paus.5.5.5

Λευκοθέα.definition: Ep. the white goddess (cf; the faculty of seeing white, Aristo Stoic.1.86

Λευκόθιον.definition: name of a building in Delos, IG11.154 A 24, al

λευκομφάλιος.definition: with white navel or centre, of fig-trees, Thphr.CP5.1.8

λεῦκος.definition: name of a fish , Theoc.Beren.4, cf. Arist.HA567a20

λεύσιμος.definition: stoning, E.Or.863; death by stoning, Id.Ion1237 ; ib.1240 ; Id.Or.50; ib.614, cf. Heracl.60; curses that will end in stoning, A.Ag.1616; stoned, ib.1118

λευστήρ.definition: one who stones, E.Tr.1039; as Adj., death by stoning, A.Th.199; . . Lyc.1187, cf. Hsch

λεχεποίη.definition: grown with grass fit to make a bed, i.e. grassy, meadowy, epith. of various towns, Il.2.697, h.Ap.224, h.Merc.88:—masc. of the river Asopus, from its grassy banks, Il.4.383, Orac. ap. Hdt.9.43.—Hom. has both forms in …

λέχος.definition: poet. Noun, couch, bed, Il.1.609, al; bier, usu. in pl., 24.589, 702, IG Rom.4.507a25 , etc

λέχριος.definition: also Call.Del.236: :—slanting, crosswise, with a Verb, S.OC195 ; E.Hec.1026 , Med.1168; X.Cyn.4.3: metaph., all the business in hand is cross, S.Ant.1345

Λεωκόρειον.definition: the temple of the daughters of Leos, Th.1.20, 6.57

λεωπετρία.definition: = D.S.3.16 , LXXEz.24.8, al.; is f.l. in Hsch.; cf

λεωσφέτερος.definition: only in Hdt.9.33, made him one of their own people, their fellow-citizen

Λήδα.definition: Leda, A.Ag.914, etc.:—the forms only Ep., as Od.11.298

λήδανον.definition: or = gum- ladanum, Hdt.3.112, cf. 107, Hp.Mul.2.189, Plu.2.397a, Ruf. ap. Gal.12.425, Heraclid. ib.436, Gal.12.28, al., Wilcken Chr.273i15 . , Plu.l.c., also Ruf. l.c.; Heraclid., Gal., WilckenChr. ll.cc., v.l. in Hp.…

λήδιον.definition: or Dim. of IG22.1514.45, 1516.23, 1517.149, 151 :—also or Men.1028, Clearch.25, Macho ap.Ath.13.582d sq., Hsch.; cj. Toup for Suid.; cf

ληΐδιος.definition: taken as booty, captive, AP6.20 , APl.4.203 , Tryph.679

λήϊτον.definition: town-hall, council-chamber, as the Achaeans of Achaea Phthiotis called it, Hdt.7.197; = acc. to Plu.Rom.26, Id.2.280a:—Hsch. has cf. Suid., Zonar.:—Hsch. also quotes = a public priestess

λῆμμα.definition: anything received, opp; in Logic, statement taken as true, assumption; esp. premiss in a syllogism, A.D.Synt.245.13; Arist.Top.101a14; ib.156a21, cf. Gell.9.16, Phld.Rh.1.9 S.; prop. the major premiss , CrinisStoic.3.…

λημνίσκος.definition: woollen fillet or ribbon, by which chaplets were fastened, IG22.1297.11 , al., Plb.18.46.12, Posidon.9 J., Plu.Sull.27, AP12.123; of ribbons attached to bird's feet, Callix.2; surgical bandage, Mnesith. ap. Orib.inc.1…

Λῆμνος.definition: Dor. Lemnos, Il.1.593, al., Od.8.283; sacred to Hephaestus, Sch.A.R.1.851, etc.: Adv. from Lemnos, Pi.P.1.52:—Adj. Lemnian, S.Ph.800, Ar.Lys.299; prov. from the wickedness of certain Lemnian women, Hdt.6.138, cf. A.Ch…

ληναῖος.definition: belonging to the wine-press; epith. of Dionysus, as god of the wine-press, D.S.3.63

ληξιπύρετος.definition: allaying fever, Asclep. ap. Gal.14.136:—also Gal.13.68, 1013

λησίμβροτος.definition: taking men unawares, cheat, thief, h.Merc.339

λῆσις.definition: = Hsch. s.v. ; f.l. for in Critias6.12 D

Λητοΐδης.definition: Aeol., Dor. son of Leto, i.e.Apollo, h.Merc.253, Hes.Sc.479, Alc.Supp.30.3:—Pi.P.1.12 has

Λητώ.definition: Dor. contr. Leto, mother of; temple of L., Arist.EE1214a2, Str.14.3.6

λίβανος.definition: frankincense-tree, Boswellia; = frankincense, in which sense it is fem. in Pi.Fr.122.3, E.Ba.144 ; but masc. in PCair.Zen.69.13 , AP6.231 , 9.93 , Edict.Diocl. ; indeterminate in Sapph.Supp.20c.2, S.Fr.1064, Anaxandr.…

λιβανωτρίς.definition: censer, Carnead. ap. Plu.2.477b, Keil-Premerstein Zweiter Bericht No.20 , Ramsay Studies in the Eastern Rom.Provinces p.319 , Hsch

λιβλάριος.definition: = Lat. lǐbrarius, scribe, secretary, BGU 423v. 3 , PFlor.71.605 , etc

λιβερτῖνος.definition: = Lat. libertinus, freedman, IG14.1781, Act.Ap.6.9:—also = Lat. libertus, Plb.30.18.4

λιβόνοτος.definition: a wind between south-west and south, Arist.Mu.394b34, Agatharch.2.7, Peripl.M.Rubr.57; cf

Λιβύη.definition: Libya, Od.4.85, 14.295, Hdt.1.46, etc.; also for Africa generally, Id.4.42, al.; the west bank of the Nile, PTaur.8.9 , PLond.1.3.8 : prov., or Arist.HA606b20, Zen.2.51:—Adv. from Libya, D.P.46, 222:—also Dor. Nic.Al.…

λευκαθίζω.definition: to be white, Hdt.8.27 , PLeid.X.84, Gloss.; of spots on the body, LXXLe.13.38; Babr.22.9; Id.45.3, cf. Ael.NA17.8, 9; of snow-clad hills, Alciphr.3.30; Epict.Gnom.43; of fluids in the eye, to be colourless, Cass.Pr.27…

λευκάκανθα.definition: white thistle, Tyrimnus; tuberous thistle, Cnicus tuberosus, Dsc.3.19, Gal.12.58, Plin.HN22.40:—in form ib.21.94, v.l. in Gal.6.623

λευκάνθεμον.definition: white-flower, like name of several plants of the genus Anthemis, Dsc.3.137, Plin.HN21.163:— also ib.22.53

λευκανθής.definition: white-blossoming, Nic.Th.530: generally, blanched, white, Pi.N.9.23 ; S.OT742, cf. AP12.165

λεύκανσις.definition: a growing white, Arist.Ph.224b15, Alex.Aphr.in Top.304.1; clarification of oil, Gal.11.484

λευκάντυξ.definition: bright-orbed, of the moon, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.20

λευκάργιλλος.definition: or of or with white clay, Str.9.5.19: as Subst., leucargilion, white clay, Plin.HN17.42

λεύκασπις.definition: white-shielded, of a Trojan, Il.22.294; of the Carians, X.HG3.2.15; of a Maced. corps, Plu.Cleom.23; in Trag. esp. of the Argives, A.Th.89 , S.Ant.106 , E.Ph.1099; Lyr.Adesp.68

λευκερινεός.definition: Att. white fig-tree, Ath.3.76c: also as Adj., of the fruit, Hermipp.68

λευκέρυθρος.definition: whitish red, Arist.Phgn.806b4; of persons, Ptol.Tetr.143

λευκερῳδιός.definition: white heron or spoonbill, Platalia leucorodius, Arist.HA593b2

λεύκη.definition: a cutaneous disease, so called from its; white poplar, Populus alba, Thphr.HP1.10.1, al.; used for chaplets, Ar.Nu.1007, Eup.14.4, D.18.260, Theoc.2.121; later Hippiatr.22

λευκίσκος.definition: a fish, white mullet, Hices. ap. Ath.7.306e, Gal.6.713

λευκίτης.definition: Dor. = II, of a ram, Theoc.5.147

λευκοβραχίων.definition: gen. with white arms or shoulders, Suid.s.v. Sch.D Il.1.55

λευκόγειος.definition: Thphr.CP2.4.4, Hsch.s.v. Str.9.5.18, Eust.332.21 :—of or with white earth, ll. cc

λευκογραφέω.definition: paint in white on a coloured ground, Arist.Po.1450b2

λευκογραφίς.definition: a kind of clay for painting white, Plin.HN27.103; = Dsc.5.134, Aët.2.16

λευκόθριξ.definition: white-haired, white, Ar.Av.971; E.Ba.112 ; Call.Cer.121; Arist.GA786a24; Str.16.4.26

λευκόϊνος.definition: made of Thphr.Od.27; of the colour of POxy.113.5

λευκόκηρος.definition: made of white wax, Id. s.v

λευκοκύμων.definition: gen. white with waves or surf, E.Or.992

λευκόλιθος.definition: made of white marble, Supp.Epigr.4.270 ; OGI510 ; IPE12.40.42 , al.; Str.5.3.8; Id.12.5.3: as Subst., IPE12.357

λευκόλινον.definition: white flax for ropes and rigging, used esp. by the Phoenicians, Hdt.7.25,34,36, Ael.NA5.3

λευκόλοφος.definition: white-crested, Anacr.82, Ar.Ra.1016; prob. on this white hill, AP7.636

λευκομέτωπος.definition: with a white forehead, Hippiatr.104; as Subst., name of a bird, PPetr.3p.152 , PGrenf.2.14b3 , etc.; PMag.Par.1.2395, 3148, cf. 2.209

λευκόνοτος.definition: the south wind which cleared the weather , Arist.Mete.362a14: distd. from Gal.16.410, 17.655

λευκοοινάριον.definition: inscription of amphorae at Pompeii, CIL4 Suppl.6564, al

λευκοπάρυφος.definition: with white-edged robe, Alexander Magnus ap.Plu.2.180e

λευκόπεπλος.definition: white-robed, Corinn.20: metaph., Lat.dies albo notandus, Hippon.32

λευκοπληθής.definition: full of persons in white, Ar.Ec.387

λευκοποίκιλος.definition: motley-white, Sch.Theoc.4.45; as Subst., name of a gem, Plin.HN37.171

λευκόπους.definition: gen. white-footed, bare-footed, E.Cyc.72 , cf. Ar.Lys.665, Anacreont.8.5

λευκόπρωκτος.definition: with white a play on the words and II.1c, conveying a notion of cowardice, Call.Com.11

λευκόπτερος.definition: white-winged, of a ship, E.Hipp.752 : generally, white, A.Pr.993; E.Tr.848

λευκοπτέρυξ.definition: = foreg., prob. l. in Ion Eleg.10

λευκόπυρρος.definition: pale-red, Arist.Col.797b13; prob. to be read for Gal.13.984

λευκόπωλος.definition: with white horses, A.Pers.386, S.Aj.673; Plu.Cam.7; epith. of the Dioscuri , Pi.P.1.66; at Thebes also of Amphion and Zethus, E.HF29; Id.Ph.606

λευκόσαρκος.definition: with white flesh, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.44, Epaenet. ap. Ath.7.312b

λευκόσπανος.definition: pale-grey, of a coloured garment, PHamb.10.20

λευκουργός.definition: worker in marble or white stone, BCH32.500 , Milet.7.60 , Princeton Exp.Inscr. Sect.B No.1170, Wiener Denkschr.44 p.31 No.70

λευκοφαής.definition: white-gleaming, E.IA1054 ; prob. in Id.Hyps. Fr.3ii 4 ; Nonn.D.15.232; cf. sq

λευκόφαιος.definition: whitish grey, ash-coloured, PHib.1.32.13 ; PCair.Zen.433.9 , cf. Ath.3.78a, Poll.7.129; prob.in Posidon.3 J

λευκόφθαλμος.definition: white-eye, name of a gem, Plin.HN37.171

λευκοφλεγματία.definition: the beginning of dropsy , dub. in Cels.3.21

λευκοφλεγματίας.definition: one of a leuco-phlegmatous; oedematous dropsy, anasarca, Gal.10.82, al

λευκόφλοιος.definition: with white husk, cj. in Posidon.3 J.; cf

λευκοφόρος.definition: white-robed, APl.2.20; bearing white grapes, Gp.5.2.2

Λευκοφρυηνή.definition: epith. of Artemis at Magn. Mae., ib.558.12 , al

λευκόχροος.definition: contr. of pale complexion, Arist.GA728a2, Aret.SD1.13, etc.: generally, white, heterocl. acc. E.Ph.322 : pl. Ptol.Geog.7.2.17:—also Hp.Epid.2.1.10, Phlp.in GA53.3

λευκόχρυσος.definition: a gem of pale gold colour, Plin.HN37.128, 171: as Adj., Lyd.Mag.3.70

λευκόχρως.definition: white-skinned, colourless, Eub.35, Alex.98.18, Theoc.Ep.2.1, Arist.Phgn.808b4

λευκόω.definition: whiten over, Aen.Tact.31.14; mostly in Pass., to be made or become white, Pi.I.4.69; whitened or plastered, Pl.Lg.785a; = I, D.46.11; Arist.Ph.185b29; of a leper, Ph.1.346; of the list of proscribed, D.C.Fr.109.12

λευκώλενος.definition: white-armed, epith. of Hera, Il.1.55, 195, etc.; of Persephone, etc., Hes.Th.913, Pi.P.3.98, etc.; of female slaves, Od.6.239, 18.198, 19.60; perh. with a play on of a useless woman, Diogenian.6.22

λευκωματίζομαι.definition: to be affected with II.2, Sch.A.Pr.499

λεύκωσις.definition: = II.2, interpol.in; whitening, Olymp.Alch.p.91 B.; of pearls, etc., PHolm.2.36, al

λευκωτής.definition: whitewasher, or whitewashed, in dat. IG12.374.46

λευχειμονέω.definition: to be clad in white, Pl.R.617c, CIG2715.8 , Str.11.11.8, Ph.1.156

λευχείμων.definition: clad in white, Phint. ap. Stob.4.23.61a; Ph.2.188, cf. Orph.H.51.11, Aristid.Or.48.31

λεύω.definition: fut. Ar.Ach.285: aor. Hdt.9.5, Th.1.106:—Pass., fut. J.Ap.2.27: aor. S.OC , Hp.Ep.27: :—stone, Th.5.60; E.El.328; S.OC435, cf. E.IA1350

λέχομαι.definition: lie down, pres. only in Hsch; causal in Act., lay asleep, lull to sleep, Il.24.635; 14.252

λεχώ.definition: contr. Cyrenaic gen. Berl.Sitzb.1927.166, dat. ib.158, IG5.713, al. , Schwyzer323 D13 : :—woman in childbed or one who has just given birth, E.El.652, 654, 1108, Ar.Ec.530, Sor.1.77, etc.; of an animal, Opp.C.3.208: p…

λήθη.definition: Dor. forgetting, forgetfulness; after Hom., of a place of oblivion in the lower world, Simon.184.6; Ar.Ra.186; Pl.R.621a, D.H.8.52; Luc.DMort.13.6, Paus.9.39.8, Aesop.168; also, of the river in Lusitania, Str.3.3.4, 5…

ληϊβοτήρ.definition: crop-consuming, crop- destroying, Suid., etc.: fem., Od.18.29

ληΐζομαι.definition: Ep.and Ion., Hes.Op.702, Hdt.4.112; plunder, despoil, esp. by raids or forays, Th.1.5, cf. 3.85, 5.115, And.1.101, etc.; X.An.4.8.23; D.S.11.88, Jul.Or.7.210a: metaph., Pl.Epin.976a

ληϊστής.definition: = Att. h.Bacch.7, Hdt.6.17, SIG38 B20 , Democr.260, A.R.1.750

ληκυθίζω.definition: declaim in a hollow voice, as though speaking into a Call.Fr.10.13 P., Phryn.PSp.86 B., Poll.4.114, 7.182: c.acc., declaim commonplaces, Str.13.1.54

ληκυθισμός.definition: hollow, affected speaking, Plu.2.1086e, Anon. ap. Suid

ληκυθιστής.definition: one who declaims in a hollow voice, S.Fr.1063

ληματιάω.definition: to be high-spirited, v.l. in Ar.l.c

λημάω.definition: only pres., to be bleared, of the eyes, Hp.Prorrh.2.18; to be blear-eyed or purblind, to have one's eyes running pumpkins, Ar.Nu.327, cf. Hsch.; Luc.Tim.2, etc.: metaph., Ar.Pl.581

λήμη.definition: a humour that gathers in the corner of the eye, rheum, Hp.VM19, Prog.2: in pl., sore eyes, Ar.Lys.301 : metaph., the eye-sore of Piraeus, of Aegina, Pericles ap.Arist.Rh.1411a15, Plu.Per.8; old prejudices that dim the…

λημματίζω.definition: place to credit, PFlor.361.7; assume, posit, premisses, A.D.Synt.101.27

λημμάτιον.definition: Dim. of Ptol.Alm.1.10, Olymp.in Mete.261.27, Dam.Pr.233, 396, al., Zonar

Ληναιών.definition: name of a month in many Greek calendars, Hes.Op.504, SIG1014.94 , etc

ληνίς.definition: a Bacchante, Eust.629.30, Suid; = 2 or 3, PTeb.414.31 ; = 4, EM478.28

ληνοβάτης.definition: one who treads the wine-vat, Him.Or.6.3, 21.6, Sammelb.5810.12 , Gloss

ληξίαρχος.definition: the officer at Athens who kept order in the Poll.8.104

ληπτέος.definition: to be taken or accepted; neut. one must take hold, Ar.Eq.603; one must undertake, X.Mem.1.7.2; one must assume in arguing, etc., Pl.Phlb.61a; one must take or choose, X.Cyr.8.1.10; . . Arist.Pol.1280a7

ληραίνω.definition: = Ph.1.77, Hsch.; f.l. for in Heraclit.15

λήρησις.definition: silly talk, trifling, Plu.2.504b, D.L.7.118; dotage of the old, Aret.SD1.6

λῄσταρχος.definition: = D.S.33.1, App.Hisp.68, Polyaen.4.9.3, Wilcken Chr.20 iv 8

λῃστεία.definition: robbery, piracy, Th.1.5, Pl.Lg.823e, etc.; X.An.7.7.9, Arist.Pol.1256a36: in pl., . . Th.8.40

λῃστεύω.definition: fut. App.Pun.116:—Pass; c.acc., spoil, plunder, Th.4.45, App.Pun.5, etc.:—Pass., Th.4.2, 5.14, D.S.l.c.; is infested by robbers, Arr.Epict.4.1.91

λῃστήρ.definition: in Hom. = , robber, esp. pirate, Od.3.73, etc.; 17.425, cf. 16.426, AP7.737, Man.3.258:—fem. Ael.NA8.19

λῃστήριον.definition: Dor. band of robbers; retreat or nest of robbers, SIG581.52 , Str.14.1.32

λῃστής.definition: metaph., S.OT535; Lyc.1143; of love, APl.4.198

λῃστοπιαστής.definition: in pl., thief-catchers, a branch of the local police in Egypt, Wilcken Chr.472.2 , PFlor.2.181

λῃστοσαλπιγκτής.definition: robber-trumpeter, of the Tyrrhenians, inventors of the trumpet, Com. word in Men.1030; in Hsch

λῃστρίς.definition: fem. of foreg., pirate vessels, D.52.5, cf. D.S.16.5, Plu.Nic.29, etc.; Id.Thes.9, cf. Herod.6.10

λιάζω.definition: v. foreg. sub fin; to be over-enthusiastic, A.D.Pron.34.27; Phot

λιβάδιον.definition: in the common dialect, a wet place, Eust.1358.54, Thom.Mag.p.223 R.; = Hsch

λιβάζω.definition: = let fall in drops, Hsch; land full of pools of water, Poll.1.238

λιβάνινος.definition: made of frankincense, Gloss; frankincense-coloured, POxy.114.5

λιβανόμαντις.definition: also one that divines from the smoke of frankincense, Eust.1346.39

λιβανόομαι.definition: Pass., to be mixed with frankincense, LXX3 Ma.5.45; occurs in Hdn.Gr.1.451

λιβανοφόρος.definition: bearing frankincense, Heraclid.Cum.4, Peripl.M.Rubr.29, Dsc.1.68 ; contributing frankincense, OGI199.20

λιβανωτίδιον.definition: Dim. of , small censer, Roussel Cultes Égyptiens p.217

λιβανωτίζω.definition: fumigate with frankincense, Str.16.4.26; to be like frankincense, Dsc.3.84

λιβανώτινος.definition: prepared with frankincense, Apollon.Herophil. ap. Ath.15.689b

λιβανωτοπώλης.definition: dealer in frankincense, Critias70 D., Cratin.Jun.1.4

Λιβυάρχης.definition: governor of region on the west bank of the Nile, PRev.Laws 37.5 ; governor of Libya, Plb.15.25.12

λιγυηχής.definition: poet. clear-sounding, AP9.308 ; Ath.Mitt.27.339; dub. in B.Scol.Oxy.4

λιγύκροτος.definition: loud-rattling, gloss on Suid.; cf. foreg

λιγυπτέρυγος.definition: chirping with the wings, of the cicada, AP7.195

λιγυρίζω.definition: sing loud or clear, Luc.Lex.2, cf. Hsch

λιγύφθογγος.definition: clear-voiced, in Hom. always epith. of heralds, Il.2.50, al., Od.2.6, etc.; Thgn.241; Ar.Av.1380; B.5.23; Id.9.10; Opp.H.5.620

λιγύφωνος.definition: clear-voiced, loud-voiced, Il.19.350, cf. h.Merc.478; also of sweet sounds, Hes.Th.275, 518; Theoc.12.7; Orph.A.5

λιθαγωγία.definition: conveyance of stone, IG12.347.37, SIG241 B87

λιθακός.definition: = Stesich.Oxy.1087.48; on the accent, v. Hdn.Gr.1.150

λιθαναβολεύς.definition: surgical instrument for extracting stone, Aët.16.110

λίθαξ.definition: as fem. Subst., = Arat.1112, Orph.A.613; of a gravestone, AP7.392 ; of a precious stone, Man.6.343; of the pumice-stone, AP6.66

λιθάργυρος.definition: litharge, lead monoxide, Nic.Al.594; as Adj., = foreg., Achae.19

λιθάριον.definition: Dim. of stone, Thphr.HP3.7.5; a gem, IG11.287 B46 , Annuario 6/7.405 , PHolm.5.4, al

λιθεία.definition: later written a sort of fine stone; collectively, precious stones, jewellery, OGI132.8 , Str.15.1.67, 16.4.22, D.S.1.46, Peripl.M.Rubr.56

λιθηγός.definition: stone-carrying vessel, PCair.Zen.176.6, PPetr.2p.43, 3p.137 , IG11.203 B97 : pl., Rev.Phil.50.70

λιθιάω.definition: only pres., suffer from the stone, Hp.Aph.4.79, al., Pl.Lg.916a, IG42.121.68 , Arist.Pr.895a37, Ruf.Ren.Ves.3, al., Philostr.VS1.25.11; Hp.Hum.12:—also which is restored in Pl. l.c., cf. Phot. s.v. also Hsch

λιθίζω.definition: look like a stone: name of a kind of carbuncle, v.l. in Callistr. ap.Plin.HN37.94

λίθινος.definition: also AP9.719, D.L.2.33:— made of stone, Hippon.10, Ibyc.22, Hdt.3.88, Th.3.68, Herod.7.109, PHib.1.27.26 , etc.; i.e. caused by seeing the Gorgon's head, Pi.P.10.48; so Antiph.166.4; but, of a statue, Hdt.2.141 ; marb…

λιθόβασις.definition: stone base of a tripod, BCH29.541

λιθοβολέω.definition: pelt with stones, stone, LXXLe.20.2, al., D.S.17.41, Ev.Matt.21.35, Plu.2.1011e:—Pass., LXXEx.8.26

λιθοβολία.definition: throwing of stones, Hp.Fract.2 (pl; stoning, Sch.A.Eu.189

λιθοβόλος.definition: throwing stones, pelting with; engine for hurling stones, Plb.8.5.2, Moschio ap.Ath.5.208c, Ath. Mech.18.6; distd. from D.S.20.48; also LXX1 Ma.6.51, J.BJ5.6.3; in full, ib.4.9.12

λιθογλυφία.definition: a cutting in stone, Man.4.130 ; cj. Rigler

λιθογλύφος.definition: sculptor, Luc.Somn.18, Gal.1.7; engraver, Dsc.5.147 ; title of play by Philemon, Did.in D.9.62

λιθογλώχιν.definition: gen. set with sharp stones, Nonn.D.40.354, cf. 6.138

λιθοδόμος.definition: mason, joiners and masons, X.Cyr.3.2.11 codd

λιθοειδής.definition: like stone, Hp.Morb.4.55, Pl.Ti.74a, Gal.2.745, etc

λιθοκέφαλος.definition: with a stone in its head, Arist.Fr.294

λιθοκόλλητος.definition: set with precious stones; inlaid work, mosaic, prob. in Str.16.4.19, cf. Thphr.Lap.35

λιθοκόπος.definition: stone-cutter, Antipho Soph.92, D.47.65, IG3.307, prob. in 3455

λιθοκρήδεμνος.definition: with crown of stone, of a cliff, Coluth.103

λιθολάβος.definition: instrument for extracting the stone, Gal.14.787

λιθόλευστος.definition: deserving to be stoned, Call.Epigr.42.5, Alex.Aet.3.12

λιθολογέω.definition: build with unworked stones, IG22.463.39; Pass., to be demolished, Aq.Mi.3.12

λιθολόγημα.definition: foundation of unworked stone, X.Cyr.6.3.25, IG 22.463.45 , 1672.47

λιθολογία.definition: laying of a foundation of unworked; heap of stones, Aq.Ps.78.1

λιθολόγος.definition: I) one who picks out stones for building: hence, one who builds with stones picked out to fit their places, not squared , BSA3.112 : so generally, mason, Pl.Lg.858b; masons and joiners, Th.6.44, cf. 7.43, X.HG4.4.18

λιθοξόος.definition: stone- or marble-mason; sculptor, Plu.2.74d, IG3.1372, AP5.14

λιθοποιέω.definition: turn to stone, v.l. in Luc.DMar.14.3

λιθοπρίστης.definition: sawing stone or marble, IG12.313.129, Poll.10.148

λιθόστρωτος.definition: paved with stones, S.Ant.1204; esp. of tessellated work, Str.17.1.28, Poll.7.121; mosaic or tessellated pavement, IG42.110.19 , LXXCa.3.10, Ev.Jo.19.13, CIG2643 , Roussel Délos: Colonie Athénienne p.422, Arr.Epict.4.7…

λιθοτομέω.definition: quarry, Ph.1.235, Philostr.VA3.48:—Pass; cut for the stone, Gal.1.168:—Pass., Dsc.5.15, Paul.Aeg.6.60

λιθοτομία.definition: Ion. stone-quarry; cutting for the stone, lithotomy, Gal.18.29, Paul. Aeg.6.60

λιθοτόμος.definition: for cutting stones; Subst., surgeon who cuts for the stone, Gal.1.125, Thras.24; but, who cuts the stone , Ammonius Cels.7.26.3

λιθουλκέω.definition: draw or quarry stones, Suid.: metaph., drag slowly along, Hsch

λιθουργέω.definition: work in stone, hew, LXXEx.35.33; turn into stone, petrify, AP3.11 , cf. Philostr.Im.1.11

λιθουργία.definition: sculpture in marble, IG12.347.39, D.S.4.76; working at or in stone, Thom.Mag.p.221 R.: in pl., stone-quarries, Brut.Ep.37

λιθοφόρος.definition: carrying stones, D.S.13.78; as Subst. = I.2, Plb.4.56.3

λιθόω.definition: only in Pass. to be petrified; prob. = Poll.7.121

λικμαῖος.definition: presiding over winnowing, of Demeter, AP6.98

λικμητήριον.definition: winnowing-fan, shovel, Sm. Je.15.7, Thd.Is.30.14, Hsch

λικμητής.definition: = PFay.101.4 , Poll.1.222, Aq., Sm.Je.51.2, Serv.Dan.ad Verg.G.1.166

λικνίτης.definition: god of the epith. of Dionysus, Orph.H.46.1, 52.3, Plu.2.365a:—fem. S.Ichn.269

λικνοφόρος.definition: carrying the sacred in procession, D.18.260, Call.Cer.127

λικνόω.definition: or = in part. dat. pl. , dub. in Ostr.Strassb.748

λιμαγχέω.definition: in Pass., to be weakened or reduced by hunger or low diet, Hp.Art.8, Prorrh.2.4, POxy.37i 14 , Gal.10.584

λιμαγχονέω.definition: = Id.Art.81, Antisth. ap. Stob.3.8.26, LXXDe.8.3, Gal.15.573

λιμένιος.definition: of the harbour, epith. of Aphrodite, Paus.2.34.11; of Zeus, Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.p.84 M.; cf. sq

λιμενίτης.definition: voc. god of the; custom-house officers, Dam.Isid.186

λιμενορμίτης.definition: god of harbours and mooring-places, epith. of Priapus, AP10.5

λιμνάς.definition: poet. fem. of Theoc.5.17, Babr.115.1, Paus.3.7.4

λιμναστής.definition: supervisor of irrigation-works, PTeb.209 , Wilcken Chr.392.4

λιμνήστινον.definition: drug prepared from II, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.92

λίμνηστις.definition: = Ps.-Dsc.3.6, cf. Aret.CA1.2, al.; = Gal.6.434:—also = Androm. ap. Gal.13.1036: gen. sg. Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.101

λιμνήτης.definition: epith. of Artemis at Limnae , IG5.1431.38 , Paus.3.23.10, 4.4.2, al., Artem.2.35, Sch.Th.Oxy.853x14: voc. AP6.280

λίμνιον.definition: Dim. of Arist.Mir.840b33, dub. in Phld.Mort.32

λιμνόβιος.definition: living in a lake, opp. Ael.NA6.10, Philum.Ven.36.1

λιμνοθάλασσα.definition: Att. lagoon, Xanth.3, Arist.HA598a20, GA761b7, Gal.6.711; later, of the Dead Sea, Aët.1Praef

λιμνομάχης.definition: candidate for the prize at the Lenaea, v. II.1, Hsch

λιμνόομαι.definition: Pass., become a marsh, Thphr.HP5.4.6, CP5.12.3, Str.5.3.13

λιμνόχαρις.definition: Grace of the marsh, or Love-marsh, name of a frog, Batr.12, 212

λιμοκίμβιξ.definition: one who starves himself from avarice, Com.Adesp.1073

λιμοκτονία.definition: Ion. treatment by abstinence from food, Hp.Acut.24, Vict.3.71, Gal.11.182: pl., Pl.Prt.354a

λιμόψωρος.definition: scurvy, arising from hunger or bad food, Plb.3.87.2:—later Hippiatr.69

λινάριον.definition: Dim. of thread, Roussel Cultes; net, D.Chr.7.71, Eust.574.32

λινικός.definition: pertaining to flax: tax on flax, PTeb.347.12

λινόδετος.definition: bound with flaxen cords, E.IT1043; Tim.Pers.85; tied by the foot, Ar.Nu.764

λινοθώραξ.definition: Ep. and Ion. wearing a linen cuirass, Il.2.529, 830; AP14.73; Str.3.3.6

λινόπλεκτος.definition: twisted or plaited of flax, Nonn.D.26.56 codd

λινόπληκτος.definition: shy of the net, of animals that have been caught and escaped, Plu.2.642a:—also Hsch.: Sup. Numen. ap. Ath.7.321b

λινόπτης.definition: one who watches nets to see whether anything is caught, Arist. ap. Sch.Ar.Pax1178, Poll.5.17, Hsch

λινόσπερμον.definition: linseed, Dsc.2.103, Gal.6.549, Artem.1.68, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.67, POxy.103.13 :—also Cleopatra ap.Gal.12.433, Hippiatr.54, Alex. Trall.12, v.l. in Gal.6.549

λινοστατέω.definition: lay nets, Opp.C.4.64, Longus2.13:— Pass., to be surrounded and caught with nets, Ath.5.219d

λινοστολία.definition: wearing of linen, linen clothing, Plu.2.352c , Man.4.344, Vett.Val.4.27

λινόστροφος.definition: twisted of flax, Opp.H.3.76; = marrubium, Plin.HN20.241, Gloss

λινουργεῖον.definition: linen factory, prob. l. in Str.4.2.2 : sg., Id.16.1.7

λινοϋφής.definition: weaving linen, EM558.49:—also AB302, PGiss.40 ii 27 , Cat.Cod.Astr.8.216, etc.; cf

λινοϋφικός.definition: pertaining to linen-weaving, POxy. 669.33; linen-weaver, BGU637.17 : tax on linen-weaving, POxy.1438.12

λινοχίτων.definition: with linen tunic, Hsch., prob. l. in Him.Or.11.1

λινόχορτος.definition: or joint crop of flax and grass, PBaden 15.20

λινυφαντεῖον.definition: workshop for weaving flax, PMagd.36.2 , PTeb.5.238

λιπαίνω.definition: aor. Opp.H.4.357; of rivers, make fat, enrich, E.Ba.575 , cf. Hec.454 ; of Sciron swallowed by a sea-tortoise, . . Euph. l. c

λιπανδρέω.definition: to be in want of men, Ephor.216 J

λιπαράμπυξ.definition: with bright fillet or headband, Pi.N.7.15; parodied by Ar.Ach.671 , as epith. of fish-sauce

λιπαρής.definition: persisting or persevering in a thing; of things, Ar.Lys.672; Luc.Abd.4; an obstinate fever, Id.Hist.Conscr.1

λιπαρία.definition: Ion. persistence, perseverance, Hdt.9.21, cf. 70; importunity, Ael.Fr.61

λιπαρίσχιος.definition: dub. sens. in Lyr. in Philol.80.338

λιπαροκρήδεμνος.definition: with bright headband, Il.18.382, h.Cer.25, 459, etc

λιπαρόχροος.definition: with shining body, sleek of skin, Theoc.2.165:— also acc. ib.102

λιπαυγής.definition: deserted by light, dark, sunless, IG12.891.5 , Orph.H.18.2; blind, AP9.13

λιπέλαιον.definition: gloss on pinguis olivi, Serv. ad Verg.E.5.68

λιπερνέω.definition: to be poor, Suid. ; to be meagre, J.AJ2.5.5:—but Hsch. has

λιπογράμματος.definition: wanting a letter, Suid. s.v. Eust.1379.55

λιπόγυιος.definition: wanting a limb, maimed, lame, AP9.13

λιπόδερμος.definition: without a skin, of ulcers, ibid.; without a foreskin, Sor.1.103; circumcised, Dsc.2.82, Crito ap. Gal.12.449, Gal.19.445, Paul.Aeg.6.53

λιποθυμέω.definition: fall into a swoon, faint, Hp.Art.68, Mul.2.134, Plu.Them.10, Gal.1.139

λιπόκωπος.definition: without handle, cj. Toup in AP6.307 for or

λιποναύτης.definition: leaving the sailors, Theoc.13.73, Anon. ap. Suid

λιπόξυλος.definition: lacking wood: metaph., defective, feeble, Emp.71.1, cf. 21.2

λιπόπαις.definition: childless, found in neut. pl., Man.4.584

λιπόπατρις.definition: leaving one's country; causing to forget one's country, i.e. the lotus, AP15.12

λιπόπτολις.definition: leaving the city, ib.9.78; Hsch. s.v. Phot. s.v

λιπόρρινος.definition: without skin, of Marsyas; epith. of the salamander, perh. with greasy skin, Nic.Al.537

λιποσαρκής.definition: = AP11.374 , Man.1.55, cj. for in Opp.C.2.106

λιπόσαρκος.definition: lean, thin, Hp.Ep.17, v.l. in Opp.C.2.106 ; of the skeleton, IG14.2131 of wounds, leaving a hollow, Hippiatr.77

λιποσιτέω.definition: to be in want of corn or bread, Suid

λιποστρατέω.definition: desert, refuse to serve in arms, Sch.Ar.Eq.226

λιποστρατία.definition: desertion from the army, refusal to serve, Hdt.5.27, Th.6.76, D.H.11.22:—also Th.1.99, Ph.2.132

λιποτακτέω.definition: desert one's post, LXX4 Ma.9.23, Ascl.Tact.3.6, Plu.2.241a; Ph.1.268

λιποτάκτης.definition: deserter, D.H.8.79, Ph.1.144, J.BJ5.3.4, Max. Tyr.9.7: metaph., Jul.Ep.183

λιποταξία.definition: desertion, D.21.166 codd. : metaph., Anatolius ap.Theol.Ar.35

λιποτάξιον.definition: desertion, Ph.2.132:—elsewh. in gen. indictment for desertion, Pl.Lg.943d, D.21.103; Lys.14.5; Com. phrase, Antiph.129.9, cf. Pl.Com.7, Ar.Fr.808, v. Poll.8.42

λιποτελέω.definition: to be in arrears with taxes, IG9.334.14

λιποψυχέω.definition: swoon, S.Fr.496, Th.4.12, X.HG5.4.58, Xenarch.7.12, Arist.Somn.Vig.456b15, D.S.12.62, Plu.2.347b, Arr.An.6.11.2

λιποψυχία.definition: swooning, v.l. in Hdt.1.86, Hp.Aph.7.8, Arist.Somn.Vig.455b5, Plu.2.695a, Arr.An.6.10.2

λίπτομαι.definition: pf. to be eager, A.Th.355 : c. gen., to be eager for, long for, ib.380:—later in Act. A.R.4.813, Lyc.131, Nic.Th.126

λιπυρία.definition: Ion. for a malignant intermittent fever, Hp.Judic.11:—also Id.Morb.2.51:—hence one who suffers from Gal.17.728, cf. 18.121, Ps.-Gal.19.399:—Adj. , like Hp.Coac.117; of the nature of Id.Ep.21

λιραίνω.definition: to be bold or shameless, = Hsch

λίστριον.definition: Dim. of sq., = Ar.Fr.809 , Hsch.; cf

λίστρον.definition: tool for levelling or smoothing, spade, shovel, Od.22.455, Lyc.1348, Mosch.4.101:—later also Sch.Nic.Th.29, EM587.43

λίσφος.definition: Att. for Moer.p.245 P.; said to; as Subst. = EM567.20

λιτανεία.definition: entreaty, LXX2 Ma.3.20, 10.16, PTeb.284.9 , Corn.ND12: pl., D.H.4.67; Jul.Ep.114, cf. Iamb.Myst.1.15

λιταργίζω.definition: Att. fut. slip away, Ar.Pax562; cf

λίταργος.definition: running quick, An.Ox.2.236, EM567.38, prob. in Semon.7.12

λιτοδίαιτος.definition: of a plain way of life, D.H.2.49

λιτρίζω.definition: weigh or deliver by weight, POxy.1543.1

λιφαιμέω.definition: lack blood, Arist.Pr.877a30, Gal.12.693; bleed to death, J.AJ8.15.5, App.Gall.10, Hsch

λιχμάζω.definition: trans., lick, Opp.H.2.250, Nonn.D.44.111; Ion. impf., Mosch.2.94

λόβιον.definition: Dim. of sq. 1.1, Gal.14.701; of sq. I.2; fruit of the Dsc.2.146

λογαριάζω.definition: calculate, Eust. ad D.P.907, Sch.Ar.Pl.381:—hence calculation, Sch.Luc.Cat.4

λογέμπορος.definition: phrase-monger, Artem.2.70: a pecul. accent is mentioned by Eust.463.40, 1447.47

λογεύς.definition: speaker, Critias54 D., Plu.2.813a; prose-writer, Sch. D.T.pp.114,119 H

λογίατρος.definition: a physician only in words, Gal.Libr.Propr.1, Id.15.159, al.:—hence Ph.1.526

λογικεύομαι.definition: to be merely arguing, Dam.Pr.320, cf. 162

λογικότης.definition: rationality, Id.19.481, Alex. Aphr.in Metaph.205.33, Eust.1953.44

λόγιον.definition: oracle, esp. one preserved from antiquity; the sayings of the Lord, LXXPs.11.6, cf.Act.Ap.7.38, Ep.Rom.3.2, 1 Ep.Pet.4.11

λογιότης.definition: eloquence, Ph.2.93, Plu.2.205a; as title, from I.2, POxy.902.13 , etc

λογιστεία.definition: office of Bull.Inst.Français d' Arch.Orient.22.193 , Inscr.Délos 396 A 19 , IG12.83 , OGI509.9 , PKlein.Form.1010 , Cod.Just.10.56.1, etc

λογιστήριον.definition: the place at Athens where the; = Arist.Fr.446; . . at the first meeting of the SIG1219.36

λογογραφέω.definition: to be a II, write speeches; make into a story, Jul.Or.7.208c

λογογραφία.definition: writing of speeches: and generally, of; office of official recorder in a law-court, PAmh.2.82.7

λογογράφος.definition: prose-writer, opp. poet; professional speech-writer, Alex.124.19, Aeschin.1.94; as a term of reproach, Pl.Phdr.257c, cf. Din.1.111, D.19.246, Aeschin.3.173, Hyp.Ath.3: but without such implication, Arist.Rh.1413b13

λογοδαιδαλία.definition: Ion. skill in adorning a speech, Aus.Ep. 10.26

λογοδαίδαλος.definition: skilled in tricking out a speech, Pl.Phdr.266e

λογοδεής.definition: wanting in reason or reasonableness, prob. l. in Arist.Spir.481b27

λογόδειπνον.definition: feast of words, learned banquet, Ath.1.b

λογοθεσία.definition: keeping of accounts, POxy.136.33 (pl; description, account, Bito44.9

λογοθέτης.definition: auditor, BGU77.10 , al., Cod.Just.10.30.4, Procop.Arc.8, al

λογοθεώρητος.definition: to be apprehended by the intellect alone, of the pores, Cael. Aur.TP3.2.19, CP2.16, cf. Cic. ap. Macr.Sat.2.3.6

λογοκλοπία.definition: stealing of another's words or thoughts, plagiarism, attributed to Empedocles by Timae.81

λογομάγειρος.definition: one who cooks up words, Suid. s.v

λογομανέω.definition: to have a passion for study, ChioEp.15.3

λογομαχία.definition: war about words, disputation, 1 Ep.Ti.6.4 , Porph. ap. Eus.PE14.10; title of Menippean satire by Varro, Nonius p.268 L., Porphyr.ad Hor.Sat.2.4

λογόμιμος.definition: writer or actor of spoken mimes, Hegesand.13

λογοποιέω.definition: write, compose, Pl.R.378d, Lg.636d; write; fabricate tales, esp. of newsmongers, Th.6.38, And.1.54, Lys.16.11, D.4.49, Thphr.Char.8.1; Lys.22.14; Plb.28.2.4:—Pass., D.C.37.35

λογοποίημα.definition: idle tale, piece of gossip, Antiph.166.2

λογοποιία.definition: tale-telling, news-mongering; tale, piece of gossip, Nic.Dam.130.20 J. , Charito3.2

λογοποιός.definition: prose-writer; esp. historian; writer of fables, Hdt.2.134, cf. Plu.Sol.28

λογότροπος.definition: a shortd. form of syllogism, CrinisStoic.3.269

λογχαῖος.definition: of or with a spear, Suid

λογχάριον.definition: Dim. of , Posidon.2 J., Luc.Hist.Conscr.25; as an ornament, POsl.46.12

λόγχη.definition: lance-shaped birth-mark, Trag.Adesp.84; lance, spear, javelin, Batr.129; Pi.N.10.60, cf. S.Tr.512 , etc.: metaph., Id.Fr.157; prov. of a bragging coward, a 'fire-eater', Timocl.12.5

λόγχιμος.definition: of a spear, the clash of spears, A.Ag.404

λογχίον.definition: small spear-head, IG22.1541.17: pl., of ornaments composing a necklace, ib.11.161 B 23, al.; small spears, Sammelb.7247.25, al

λογχίτης.definition: spearman, Hdn.Epim.78; plant with spear-shaped seeds, Serapias Lingua, Dsc.3.144, Gal.12.63

λογχοδρέπανον.definition: spear with sickle-shaped head, partisan, Suid. s.v. Sch.Lyc.836

λογχόομαι.definition: Pass., to be furnished with a point or head, Arist.EN1111a13; Str.3.5.1; to be ornamented with Lyd.Mag.2.4

λογχοφόρος.definition: spear-bearing, Id.Hec.1089: as Subst. spearman, pikeman, Ar.Pax1294, X.Cyr.2.1.5, Plb.3.84.14, POxy.1241 ii 16 ; Sammelb.6154.6 , Bull.Soc.Alex.7.64

λοιβαῖος.definition: of or belonging to a Megaclid. ap. Ath.12.512f

λοιβεῖον.definition: cup for pouring libations, Plu.Aem.33, Marc.2

λοίγιος.definition: pestilent, deadly, Il.1.518, 573; I think there shall be sorrow, 21.533, 23.310; A.R.1.469: neut. pl. of poisons, Androm. ap. Gal.14.37

λοίδορος.definition: railing, abusive, E.Cyc.534; as Subst. railer, 1 Ep.Cor.5.11, Plu.2.177d: = Arist.Phgn.808b37, Plu.2.810d; AP5.175

λοίμιος.definition: = foreg., epith. of Apollo at Lindos, Macr.Sat.1.17.15

λοιμώσσω.definition: Att. fut. to have the plague, Gal.10.362, Luc.Hist.Conscr.15, Scyth.2, Max.Tyr.41.4, Sch.Ar.Pl.627; also a plague-spot, Procl.in Alc.p.256 C

λοιπαδάριος.definition: one who is in arrear with taxes, POxy.136.33

λοιπάζω.definition: leave, Gloss.:—Pass., to be left over, remain, POxy.1194.3 , Sch.Ar.Pl.227, etc.; to be in need, Anon.in EN448.23

λοιπογραφέω.definition: allow to remain in arrear, carry over a debt, PPetr.3p.154 , PTeb.112.34, al. , CIG2335.23 , BGU362 iii 21, al. , Nech. ap. Vett.Val.279.12

λοιπογραφία.definition: outstanding debt, arrears, BGU567.2; carrying over of debt or arrears, PStrassb.77.5

λοίσθιος.definition: S.Ant.895, etc.; also A.Ch.500:—= sq., Pi.P.4.266, A.Ag.120 , S.Ant.1220, etc.; Id.OC583: neut. as Adv., last. Id.Aj.468, Ant.1304; A.R.2.559; E.HF23; Theoc.5.13

λοξοειδής.definition: oblique, of the lower ribs, Ruf.Oss.25

λοξόπορος.definition: moving aslant, of the Moon, Hymn.Is.30

λοξότης.definition: obliquity, Str.2.1.37, Placit.5.9.2; ambiguity, of oracles, Plu.2.409c

λοπαδεύω.definition: dress as a dish, Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.25, AB105

λοπάδιον.definition: Dim. of 2, Ar.Pl.812, Eub.9,38; oyster, Gp.20.18

λόπιμος.definition: easily stripped, of nuts which have a skin and not a shell, Nic.Fr.76, Sor. ap. Gal.12.420, cf. Gal.6.621, Hsch

λόρδωσις.definition: a curvature of the spine which is convex in front, Hp.Art.48, Gal.18.493, Sch.Theoc.5.43

λουτήρ.definition: washing or bathing-tub, Supp.Epigr.4.263.10 , CIG2820 A 10 , IGRom.4.454 , Callix.2, Moschio ap.Ath.5.207f, LXXEx.30.18, al

λουτηρίδιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., HeroSpir.1.37, BGU781 ii 12 , Dsc.1.43

λουτήριον.definition: Dor. Tab.Heracl.1.184, =; a kind of cup, Epig.6

λόφουρος.definition: in neut. pl., pack-animals, as horse, ass, mule, Arist.HA491a1, GA755b18, IG 12.677.23 ; also called Arist.Pr.895b12 ; Thphr.HP5.7.6; opp. ib.3.10.2, cf. 2.7.4. Arist.Pr.l.c

λοχαγία.definition: Dor. for rank or office of X.An.1.4.15, 3.1.30, Arist.Pol.1322b4

λοχαῖος.definition: bearing down, like heavy ears of corn, Phot., cf. Hsch.; and so prob. in Thphr.CP3.21.5, 23.5: hence metaph., richly-blooming, Arat.1057

λοχεῖος.definition: title of Artemis, = IG9.141, 142 , Orph.H.36.3, etc

λόχευμα.definition: that which is born, child, E.Ion921; in pl., = child-birth, E.El.1124: metaph., in the bursting of the bud, A.Ag.1392

λοχεύτρια.definition: woman in childbed, metaph. as Adj; midwife, Sch.DIl.16.187

λοχεύω.definition: bring forth, bear; of the midwife, bring to the birth, deliver, E.Ion948, 1596, cf. El.1129:—hence in Pass., to be brought to bed, be in labour, Id.Tr.602 ; of Semele, Id.Ba.3, cf. Plu.Pel.16: c. gen., Id.Cic.2

λοχίζω.definition: = lie in wait for:—Pass; place in ambush, Th.3.107; D.H.2.55: c. dat. loci, Id.3.64 ; is prob. l. in Plu.Oth.7

λοχίτης.definition: one of the same or company; one who lies in wait, Hsch., Suid

λοχμάζω.definition: to be downy, Pisand. ap. Sch.T Il.4.147

λοχμαῖος.definition: of the coppice, of the nightingale, Ar.Av.737

λόχμη.definition: thicket, copse, esp. as the lair of wild beasts, Od.19.439; Pi.O.6.40, cf. P.4.244; S.Ichn.121: in pl., lying in wait in the coppice, Pi.O.10.30; Ar.Ec.61, cf. Lys.800: prov., Sch.Ar.V.922: also in Prose, Arist.HA615a…

λυάω.definition: = Call.Aet.Oxy.2080.76, cf. Choerob.in Theod.2.162 H.:—Med., Hsch

λύγδινος.definition: of white marble, Africa; marble-white, AP5.12 ; Anacreont.15.27

λύγδος.definition: white marble, Peripl.M.Rubr.24; AP5.27 ; ib.193 ; D.S.2.52, cf. Mart.6.13, 42

λύγινος.definition: of agnus castus, Heph. ap. Ath.15.673e; cf

λυγισμός.definition: a bending, twisting, like the willow, hence of wrestlers, Luc.Anach.24, cj. in Philostr.Im.2.6 ; of dancers, Id.VA4.21; PMich.in Class.Phil.22.10: metaph., of the windings and twistings of a sophist, Ar.Ra.775

λυγόδεσμος.definition: bound with willow-twigs, epith. of Artemis, Paus.3.16.11

Λυδίζω.definition: speak Lydian, Hippon. in PSI9.1089.1; play the Lydian, of Magnes, in reference to his play called Ar.Eq.523; Philostr.VA5.32:—in Phot. and Suid. also

λύθρον.definition: or defilement from blood, gore, Hom., only in dat., . . Il.11.169, 20.503; 6.268, Od.22.402: masc. AP9.323 , Ph. ap.Gal.13.268, Poll.1.46, M.Ant.3.3, Jul.Or.2.71a: the neut. only in APl.4.112: in Medic., of the impure…

λυκηθμός.definition: a wolf's howl, formed like Anon. ap. Suid

Λυκιάρχης.definition: president of the of Lycians, Str.14.3.3, OGI 495.14 , 568 :—hence ib.556 , etc.; and TAM2.190.5 , etc

λυκόβρωτος.definition: eaten by wolves, Arist.HA596b7, Plu.2.642b, Orib.Eup.4.88.11; perh. to be read in Hsch. s.v. cf

λυκοθαρσής.definition: not fearing wolves, AP7.703 ; in Hsch

λυκοκτόνος.definition: wolf-slaying, epith. of Apollo; wolf's-bane, aconitum, Gal.11.820

λυκοπάνθηρος.definition: wolf-panther, synon. of in Hdn.Epim.60, cf. Eust.856.51

λυκοπέρσιον.definition: an Egyptian plant, with a strong- smelling, yellowish juice, Hyoscyamus muticus, Gal.11.682

λυκοσπάς.definition: torn by wolves, epith. of bees; of horses, Call.Fr.474, where it may mean drawn by the bit , cf. Plu.2.641f, or as expld. by Choerob.in Theod.1.287, cf. Plu. l. c. ; but were a breed of horses in lower Italy, = Phot.,…

λυκόστομος.definition: wolf-mouth, a kind of anchovy, = Ael.NA8.18, Gp.20.46.1

λυκοφίλιος.definition: like wolf's friendship, Men.833. Adv. Ael.Dion.Fr.251

λυκοφόρος.definition: branded with the mark of a wolf, name of a swift breed of Venetian horses , Str.5.1.9

λυκόω.definition: tear like a wolf:—Pass., to be torn by wolves, X.Cyr.8.3.41

λυμαίνομαι.definition: cleanse from dirt, of fullers, Hp.Vict.1.14; v; c. acc., outrage, maltreat, . . Hdt.5.33; Id.8.28; S.OC855; dishonour . . , E.Ba.354: c. acc. cogn. added, . . . . Ar.Av.100; E.Hel.1099; also in Att. Prose, Lys.30.26, …

λυμαντήριος.definition: injurious, destructive, A.Pr.991: c. gen., destroying, ruining, Id.Ag.1438; Id.Ch.764

λυμαντής.definition: = foreg., S.Tr.793: also Muson.Fr.8p.34H., Epict.Gnom.9: c. gen., Arr.Epict.3.7.20; Ph.2.429

λυμεών.definition: destroyer, corrupter, S.Aj.573; E.Hipp.1068; Isoc.8.141, cf. 4.80; Tim.Pers.81; of robbers, E.Fr.260, cf. J.BJ4.3.9; X.Hier.6.6; SIG799.23 ; of bad physicians, Gal.9.916; . . Jul.Or.2.87a; Id.Gal.93d

λυπέω.definition: grieve, vex, whether in body or mind; abs., cause pain or grief, S.Aj.589, Ant.573, cf. OT1231; Antiph.107, Men.410

λύπημα.definition: pain, Antipho Soph.49 , D.C.55.17, f.l. in S.Tr.554

λυπρότης.definition: wretchedness, poverty, of land, Str.2.5.32, al

λυραοιδός.definition: one who sings to the lyre, AP7.612 , APl.4.279:—contr. AP6.118 , Plu.Sull.33: Adj. Callistr.Stat.7

λυριστής.definition: player on the lyre, Plin.Ep.9.17.3, Artem.4.72; un-Att. acc. to Hellad. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.529 B.:—fem. Sch.Juv.11.162

λυρογηθής.definition: delighting in the lyre, AP9.525.12, An.Par.4.350

λυρόδμητος.definition: lyre-built, epith. of Thebes, Nonn.D.25.415, al

λυροκτυπία.definition: a striking of the lyre, ib.6.54.10 , APl.4.277

λυρόκτυπος.definition: striking the lyre, IG14.2134.6; twanging like a lyre, of a bow-string, Lyc.918

λυρῳδία.definition: song to be sung to the lyre, Poll.4.58, Aristid.Or.37.21, Callistr.Stat.7

λυσανίας.definition: ending sorrow, Ar.Nu.1162 , cf. Hsch.; dub. cj. in Theopomp.Com.30.4

λυσίζωνος.definition: of a soldier, unequipped, ungirded; loosing the zone, i.e. ceasing to be a maid, Hsch., Suid.: hence as epith. of Eileithyia and Artemis, who assisted women in travail, Theoc.17.60, Corn.ND34, Orph.H.2.7, 36.5, etc

λυσιμάχειος.definition: Subst. loosestrife, Lysimachia vulgaris, Dsc.4.3, Gal.12.64; also Paul.Aeg.7.3

λυσιμελής.definition: limb-relaxing, epith. of sleep, Od.20.57, 23.343, Mosch.2.4, etc.; of love, Hes.Th.911, Archil.85, Sapph.40, etc.; of thirst, Thgn.838; of death, E.Supp.47 ; of wine, sickness, etc., AP11.414 ; of the Furies. Orph.H.70.9

λυσιμέριμνος.definition: driving care away, of Dionysus, AP9.524.12; of Hermes, Orph.H.28.6; of Artemis, ib.36.5; of Sleep, ib.85.5, etc

λυσιπαίγμων.definition: gen. letting loose, i.e. giving, play or sport, Anacreont.48.9. compd. with have Herm. suggested

λυσιπήμων.definition: gen. ending sorrow or pain, Orph.H.2.11, 59.20 codd

λυσιπόλεμος.definition: name of a war-engine invented by Dorion, Pap.in Abh. Berl.Akad.1904.9

λυσιπόνιον.definition: a medicinal unguent, Gal.12.771, Alex.Trall.1.16: also an eye-salve, CIL13.10021.174, cf. 52, 63

λυσίπονος.definition: releasing from toil, labour- lightening, Pi.P.4.41; death that frees from care, Id.Fr.131.1

λυσισωματέω.definition: to be relaxed in body, Hp.Epid.5.82

λυσιτέλεια.definition: advantage, profit, Thphr. ap. D.L.5.54, D.S.1.36, LXX2 Ma.2.27, J.AJ16.9.1; economy in respect of time, i.e. by postponement of payments until they fell due, Plb.31.27.11; for the sake of economy, Dsc.5.8.—Rejected by…

λυσιτελέω.definition: prop. indemnify for expenses incurred, or; mostly impers., it profits me, is better for me, c. part., Lys.25.27; Pl.Alc.1.113d: c. inf., Id.Tht.181b; thinking it better to be dead than alive, And.1.125, cf. Pl.R.407a,…

λυσσάω.definition: Att. Ep. part. Man.1.244; rave, be mad, S.OT1258, Ant.492, Pl.R.329c, Epicur.Sent.Vat.11, Man., AP ll.cc., etc.; Ps.-Phoc.214; Pl.R.586c: c. inf., desire madly to do, Hld.2.20

λύσσημα.definition: fit of madness: in pl., ravings, E.Or.270

λυσσητήρ.definition: one that is raging or raving mad, Il.8.299; AP5.265

λυσσόδηκτος.definition: bitten by a mad dog, Dsc.1.100 , Gp.12.17.14, Heras ap.Gal.13.431, M.Ant.6.57, Damocr. ap. Aët.15.14

λυσσοδίωκτος.definition: pursued by madness, Orac. ap. X.Eph.1.6

λυτήριος.definition: loosing, delivering, A.Th.175; Subst. = the atonement or reward for all costs, Pi.P.5.106; expiatory offering, A.R.4.704

λύτρον.definition: price of release; ransom, mostly in pl. , the tithe of the ransom-money, Hdt.5.77; title of Il.24 and of play by Aeschylus; receive as ransom for . . , Th.6.5; Pl.R.393d; pay ransom, D.53.11, 13; contribute towards it…

λυτρόω.definition: release on receipt of a ransom, hold to; Pass., to be released from an obligation, PEleph.19.8

λύτρωσις.definition: ransoming, Plu.Arat.11; release, discharge from an obligation, POxy.1130.20

λυχνάπτης.definition: gloss on Hsch.: pl. misspelt POxy.1453.4, 8

λυχναψία.definition: acc. to Ath.15.701b less common form for Cephisod.11, cf. PAmh.2.70.10 , IGRom.4.1176 , etc

λυχνεῖον.definition: lampstand, Pherecr.85, IG22.1425.368, 4.1588.3 , 11.161 C77, al. ; stand for ballot-balls, Arist.Ath.68.4; cf. Ar.Frr.14, 281, Crates Com.3, Hermipp.62

λυχνία.definition: lampstand, SIG1106.118 , IG11.161 C66, 68 , LXXEx.25.30, al., PGrenf.1.14.6 , Ev.Matt.5.15, Plu.Dio9, Luc.Asin.40, etc.: condemned by Phryn.289

λυχνιαῖος.definition: belonging to a lamp, S.E.P.1.119, cf. Gal.17.413, Olymp.in Mete.18.12, al

λυχνῖτις.definition: candlewick, Verbascum mallophorum, the leaves of which served as lampwicks, Plin.HN25.121, BGU485.10 ; = Dsc.4.103

λυχνοκαΐα.definition: Ion. lighting of lamps, illumination, Cratin.227 , D.C.79.16; a Feast of Lanterns at Sais, Hdt.2.62, J.Ap.2.9

λυχνοκαυτέω.definition: light lamps, D.C.63.20: a pecul. form = in Telecl.60

λυχνομαντεία.definition: divination by means of a lamp, PMag.Lond.121.540, 556 , PMag.Par.1.952

λυχνοποιός.definition: maker of lamps or lanterns, Ar.Pax690, Philetaer.4, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.215

λυχνοπωλέω.definition: deal in lamps or lanterns, Sch.Luc.Tim.30

λυχνοπώλης.definition: dealer in lamps or lanterns, Ar.Eq.739

λυχνοφόρος.definition: carrying a lamp, Posidon.36 J., Plu.Pomp.52, J.Ap.2.9

λῶ.definition: Dor. Verb, = 1sg. indic., Ar.Lys.981; 2sg., = Epich.170.7, 172.4, Ar.Ach.766, cf. 776; Epich.171.10; Ar.Lys.95; Crates Com.41 ; Call.Dian.19; . . . . Theoc.1.12; 3sg., . . Epich.170.8: 1pl., . . Ar.Lys.1162; 3pl., Epi…

λώβη.definition: outrage, dishonour, 18.225; of persons, a disgrace, Il.3.42, cf. E.El.165 , Herod.7.95; of the Grammarians, AP11.322 ; no insult to the Arcadians, Alc.38

λωβήμων.definition: gen. = foreg., in acc. sg., Nic.Al.536

λωβήτωρ.definition: = Opp.H.4.684, AP6.168 , etc.: as fem., v.l. for in Nic.Al.536

λώπη.definition: covering, robe, mantle, Od.13.224, cf. Theoc.25.254, A.R.2.32:—also Alc.Supp.18.2 , Hippon.3, Anacr.80, Herod.8.36, Theoc.14.66, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.22.—Only poetic in class. writers, though prose writers have the derivs

λωπίζω.definition: uncover, strip, Hsch., Suid.: found only in compds. etc.; S.Tr.925, belongs to

λωποδυτέω.definition: steal clothes, esp. from bathers or; generally, rob, plunder, Ar.Ec.565,Pl.165, Diph.32.14, LXX IEs.4.24: c. acc. pers., Ar.Ra.1075, D.9.22; of plagiarists, AP11.130

λωποδύτης.definition: clothes-stealer, esp. one who; generally, thief, robber, footpad, IG12.44.5, Antipho5.9, Cratin.206, Ar.Av.497, Ra.772, Lys.10.10, Phld.Rh.2.144 S., etc.; D.4.47; plagiarist, AP11.130 , cf. Arr.Epict.2.19.28

λωροτόμος.definition: cutting thongs, Hsch. s.v. Sch.Pl.Grg.517e, Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.216

λωτίζομαι.definition: cull the best, A.Supp.963; S.Fr.724 :—Act. in Hsch

λώτινος.definition: made of lotus-wood, Anacr.39; Theoc.24.45; Ath.4.182d: hence of flutes, E.Fr.931

λωτομήτρα.definition: fruit-pulp of II, Plin. HN22.56, PMag.Par.1.754

λάθρῃ.definition: Att. Adv., secretly, by; c. gen., unknown to one, Il.5.269; Hdt.8.112, cf. 9.90, S.OT787, OC354, Ar.V.347, X.An.1.3.8.—Freq. written in codd. and Pap., but in UPZ19.28 and in some of the best codd., as the Laurentian …

λανθανόντως.definition: Adv. pres. part. of secretly, Gal.12.292, Hdn.7.9.11, 8.7.3, D.C.66.5

λάξ.definition: Adv. with the foot, Il.6.65, cf. 16.503; 5.620, 16.863; 10.158, Od.15.45; 17.233; Archil.Supp.2.13; so later Thgn.815; Id.847; to be trodden under foot, A.Eu.110, Ch.644 ; Id.Eu.542 ; A.R.2.106; Philem.1.6 D.: also in…

λεληθότως.definition: Adv. pf. part. of imperceptibly, Pl.Ax.365c, Cic.Att.6.5.3, Fam.9.2.3, D.H.Comp.22, Anacreont.15.16, Luc.Am.13; secretly, LXX2 Ma.6.11, 8.1

λελογισμένως.definition: Adv., according to calculation, . . Hdt.3.104; E.IA1021; Plu.Galb.5

λελυμένως.definition: Adv., mildly, chronically, of fever, Hp.Coac.470, cf. Gal.16.672; openly, freely, ChioEp.7.3

λέως.definition: or Ion. Adv. entirely, wholly, at all, Archil.112, cf. Hp. ap. Erot.et Gal.19.118:—elsewh. only found in the compds. ; or utterly destroyed, Theognost.Can.9, Hsch., Phot.: utterly destroyed, Hsch. : v.l. for S.Ant.127…

λίαν.definition: [v. fin.], Ion. and Ep. Adv. very; after Hom., Archil.66.7, cf. Sol.6; Anacr. ap. Ptol.Ascal.p.409 H.; to believe implicitly, Hdt.4.96; Pi.P.1.90; S.El.1172, cf. E.Med.158 ; POxy.936.13 ; Ar.Eq.1231; Lys.24.15; Pl.Prt…

λίγα.definition: Adv. of , in loud, clear tone, Il.19.284, cf. Od.8.527; in clear, sweet tone, 10.254, cf. Alcm.59, Thgn.939; A.R.4.837

λύγδην.definition: Adv., with sobs, S.OC1621, cf. AP15.28

Λυδιστί.definition: Adv. after the Lydian fashion, Cratin.256; in Music, in the Lydian mode, Pl.La.188d; Id.R.398e, cf. Arist.Pol.1342b32, Plu.2.1134b

λυσιτελούντως.definition: Adv. usefully, profitably, X.Oec.20.21, Pl.Alc.2.146b; D.C.56.40
